description: Stage four DataArray rows, columns and cell editing, with one accepted interaction per undo step and cancellation without native writes.
changes: DataArray table rendering has no native SDK or EditorState access. It reads array queries and executes the same registered commands as external modules. The existing Setup window hosts this table fragment until its later view migration.

Editor C interface version 14 passes EditorRequest to beginEdit/drawProperty. Row/column arguments and query metadata are copied into the draft. Final writes check the captured document revision and complete array identity; cancelled, closed, reordered and replaced drafts cannot address another cell. Existing provider reconfiguration refuses open host drafts.

Cells retain the existing native text representation and registered string renderer. Column name/type/parameter type share one record draft. Child combo acceptance does not submit the containing column dialog. Record members are matched by name.
All row/column menus and keyboard operations use array commands. Successful operations alone move or clear table selection. Long cell strings use dynamic storage.

Dedicated DataArray undo records store columns, rows, complete object references and native parameter states. They keep owned and shortcut parameter identities across value edits, structural edits, replay and failure recovery, without recreating placeholder parameters. Referenced objects in native chunks are retained through the existing history collector.

Native deletion temporarily detaches owned cell parameters only for destructive operations. Owners are restored after the protected native call, including failure. Cell setters see their original native owners. Batch rejection or a string-function error restores all affected values and history.

Object and parameter native text setters report FALSE after writing; their typed setters provide the actual result. Parameter copying propagates CopyValue errors. The parameter clipboard can still paste values from a removed retained source. Shortcuts require live source objects.
Cancelling a clipped cell also clears ImGui deferred deactivation text. Scrolling, object changes and window close cannot recreate and submit the cancelled draft.
Runtime SDK, file formats and production GPU rendering/transfer files remain unchanged.

checks.core_cases: Repeated draft updates with one acceptance; cancel/no-change/Redo; atomic unique-key and parameter-string-function rejection; parameter/object cells; row/column structural replay with original parameter identities; full-reference retention and eviction; stale reordered drafts; required parameter type validation; insertion destination; record member ordering; long strings; owner close; and copy/remove/paste from the parameter clipboard.
checks.public_headers: Independent C/C++ consumers check request-based begin/draw signatures, copied row positions, version 14 and identical layouts without STL, SDK, SDL or ImGui headers.

prior_failures.reason: The initial UI test ID calculation omitted the table ID stack. The column compound renderer also propagated child combo acceptance; it now waits for the containing dialog confirmation.

The external-provider test attempted reconfiguration during an open host draft. The existing refusal is retained and now explicitly tested; completed/cancelled interactions may select another provider.
The new UI test-to-table include needed its explicit S32 -> S47 dependency.
ImGui continues drawing a clipped active row. Cancelling only undrawn rows did not finish its draft.
After cancellation, ImGui could replay deactivation text into a new draft. Cancellation now drops that deferred text before drawing the same cell again.
A broad name filter also ran create/sound cases without their normal fresh-document/sample setup. Their normal CTest groups pass; final verification runs complete groups.

checks.native_cleanup: Previously reported native file-menu cleanup crashes did not reproduce in the complete runs; no root-cause fix is claimed.

performance.scope: Unchanged cubes64 scene, fixed size, Release, eleven paired groups, at least fifteen seconds of warmup per process and one second per group. No builds or CTest ran during capture.
performance.reference_preparation: Before editing, git archive froze ba89e31, and the built runtime/lib directories were copied. The copied CMakeCache identifies the frozen source. Both source and binary hashes identify the measured programs.
performance.sdk_change_option: --sdk-change allows only the inherited dirty SDK state; this task does not modify the SDK. All sixteen recursive repository states and twenty-two runtime fingerprints match.

prior_source_capture.scope: Before the clipboard-retention correction. Not final acceptance: reference MAD exceeded the original 3% limit. All samples retained.

performance.unmeasured: Application allocations, GPU-only preserve/pass/submit counts and retain/native-query counts remain unmeasured. No additional zero-allocation or all-counter claim.

remaining: The Setup window host, remaining Setup/Schematic/Layout editing and phase-four work remain; completed_phase stays three.
Cross-platform runs and the previously listed GPU/allocation counters retain their existing gaps.
The previously reported native cleanup fault remains unresolved.
